info.name: Bike Rent - Auth & FCM (User + Vendor)
info.description:
OTP login and FCM token registration for the Bike Rent User app and Vendor app.

How to use:
1. Import this collection AND the accompanying environment file (BikeRent-Auth-FCM.postman_environment.json).
2. Select the imported environment (top-right dropdown in Postman) before sending any request.
3. Run requests top-to-bottom inside each folder — each request's test script auto-saves the OTP / accessToken into environment variables used by the next request.

IMPORTANT for the Flutter app:
- The FCM token itself is generated on-device by the firebase_messaging Flutter package (FirebaseMessaging.instance.getToken()). Postman cannot generate a real one. Use a placeholder value in {{fcm_token_mobile}} to test the API shape, then swap in the real token string from the device in the actual app.
- Backend only accepts platform values "web" or "mobile". Flutter apps must always send platform: "mobile".

item.name: 1. User App (Customer)
item.description: Bike Rent customers use the platform-wide User auth (shared with the Food app) — there is no bike-rent-specific user login. FCM token can be sent inline at verify-otp, or saved/updated later via the dedicated /fcm-tokens endpoints (recommended, since verify-otp only happens once per session but the FCM token can rotate at any time).

request.description:
phone: 8–15 digit mobile number OR an email address.

In non-production (or when USE_DEFAULT_OTP=true on the backend), the response body echoes the OTP directly under data.otp so you don't need real SMS to test.

otp: exactly 4 digits, from step 1.1's response (or real SMS in production).
fcmToken / platform / name are ALL OPTIONAL — omit fcmToken+platform entirely if you just want to log in without registering a device token here (use the dedicated save-token request in 1.3 instead, which is the better pattern for a mobile app since the token can be (re)sent any time after login, not just once at login).
platform must be "web" or "mobile" — Flutter must send "mobile".

Response: { accessToken, refreshToken, user, isNewUser }

item.name: 1.3 Save / Update FCM Token (User, mobile) — RECOMMENDED for Flutter

request.description:
Requires login first (Bearer accessToken from 1.2).
Call this any time the app obtains/refreshes an FCM token from FirebaseMessaging.instance.getToken() or onTokenRefresh — not just at login.
Stores into FoodUser.fcmTokenMobile (array, de-duplicated, upserted).

Response: { success, message: 'Mobile FCM token saved successfully', data: { ownerType: 'USER', ownerId, platform: 'mobile' } }

item.name: 1.4 Remove FCM Token (User) — call on logout

request.description: Call on logout so this device stops receiving push notifications for the logged-out account. Token also accepted in the URL param or the body — either works.

item.name: 2. Vendor App (Bike Rent)
item.description: Bike-rent-specific vendor auth. IMPORTANT: unlike the User app, there is NO standalone 'save FCM token' endpoint for vendors. The FCM token can ONLY be registered by passing it inline in the verify-otp call below (2.2). If the Flutter vendor app's FCM token rotates after login, there is currently no API to update it — flag this to your backend team if you need it, or re-run verify-otp (which will re-log the vendor in) to push a fresh token.

request.description:
phone: 10-digit mobile number.

In non-production (or USE_DEFAULT_OTP=true), response echoes data.otp for testing without real SMS.

otp: from step 2.1's response.
fcmToken is OPTIONAL but this is the ONLY way to register it for a vendor — there's no separate save-token route (see folder description). No 'platform' field exists here; whatever string you send is stored as-is in BikeVendor.fcmTokens.

Response (existing vendor): { accessToken, refreshToken, vendor }
Response (brand-new phone number): { needsRegistration: true, phone, resumeStep, accessToken, refreshToken } — the vendor still needs to complete onboarding before they're a full vendor.
